summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant, and recurrent urinary tract infections was admitted with fevers, chills, and malaise. She had been treated at an outside hospital with vancomycin and cefepime for suspected urosepsis. Upon transfer, she was continued on immunosuppressive therapy and switched to IV ceftriaxone based on prior sensitivities. Urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, which was pan-sensitive, allowing transition to oral ciprofloxacin. She remained afebrile for over 24 hours, with stable renal function and improving labs. She was discharged home to complete a 14-day course of ciprofloxacin, with plans to reassess UTI prophylaxis. Her transplant team will monitor cyclosporine levels and kidney function in follow-up.
